To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N-OH-A4ABP modified DNA exhibits structural and conformational changes and is genotoxic.
4-ABPhy metabolite, N-OH-AABBPhy, is genotoxic and can damage human DNA.
N-OH-AcAABP modified DNA exhibits structural changes, is genotoxic and can induce antibodies in bladder cancer patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the genotoxic effects of a reactive metabolite, N-OH-AABB on human DNA and its possible implications in the development of bladder cancer.
the elucidation of the genotoxicity of N-hydroxy-AABP, a reactive metabolite, on human DNA and its implication in the generation of specific antibodies in bladder cancer.
the genotoxic effects of N-OH AABP and its possible role in the generation of neo-antigen in bladder cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N-OH-4-AcABP modified DNA is immunogenic, as evidenced by the production of antibodies in bladder patients and that the antibodies generated against the modified DNA are capable of recognizing the native DNA from the same patients.
4-ABPs, which are known to be involved in bladder cancer, induce the formation of neo-epitopes that are recognized by antibodies in bladder cancer.
the N-hydroxy metabolite of 3,4-dihydroxybenzidine (N-OH-DHB) is a more potent carcinogen than N-OH-4ABP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
4-ABPs are genotoxic and carcinogenic in nature, which can be used to identify and differentiate bladder cancer patients from healthy individuals by immunological methods.

the N-OH-AAABP-modified human DNA is genotoxic and the antibodies raised against this DNA can recognize the DNA obtained from bladder cancer patients, thus implicating the involvement of N-OH-4-ABP in the generation of neo-epitopes in bladder cancer.
N-OH-AABB modified DNA is genotoxic and induces neo-epitopes in the DNA which can lead to the generation of antibodies that can be used as biomarkers for bladder cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N-OH-AABB-modified DNA can be used as a potential antigen to induce antibodies against 4-ABPA-modified DNA.
the N-OH-4ABP-modified guanine base in human DNA could act as neo-epitope and induce antibodies that can specifically recognize DNA isolated from bladder carcinoma.
the DNA isolated from patients of bladder cancer could be used as a source of neo-epitopes that can be exploited for the development of a novel immunodiagnostic test.
